title: Northbridge Industrial private deploy transition playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working draft playbook for the Northbridge Industrial private deployment (VPC + on-prem connector). Audience: SRE/Platform eng, Solutions Eng, Northbridge infra owners, and our Professional Services team. Goal is to capture sizing assumptions, terraform module notes, an upgrade/cutover runbook, and open architecture Q&A before the formal runbook is produced.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Northbridge expects a phased Private deployment: stage (dev) in their VPC, pilot (pre-prod) on a pair of on-prem racks via colo, and production in their primary on-prem data center with a dedicated Redwood Private control plane. Based on workload profile (bursty inference with periodic large-batch embedding jobs), recommended initial capacity is 4x A10G-equivalent GPUs for inference nodes behind autoscaling pools plus 1x A100-equivalent for periodic heavy batch jobs. Network and storage decisions prioritize low-latency access to internal data stores and HSM/KMS for model keys. This draft documents assumptions, terraform approach, cutover steps, and risks.

Scope and exclusions:
- In scope: VPC networking, VPN/Direct Connect design, Terraform modules for private deployment, VM/GPU sizing, KMS/HSM integration, monitoring & alerting baseline, canary rollout strategy, rollback steps.
- Out of scope: model training workloads, customer DB schema changes, application-level integration beyond simple sample clients.

Customer constraints and assumptions:
- Northbridge will provide an L3 network contact and two IP subnets for Redwood control plane and runtime lanes.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 120ms for 256-token averages.
- Typical concurrent requests: 140 steady, spiky bursts to 900 for 5-10 minute windows, nightly 2-hour embedding jobs producing 50M tokens.
- Data residency: all logs and tensors retained in-customer; we will not export raw request payloads off-prem.
- KMS: customer uses AWS CloudHSM in their VPC for signing and key encryption.

Sizing rationale (initial, pilot, prod):
- Control plane: 2 x m5.4x (or equivalent) for HA; 2 vCPUs per control service container, 16 GB RAM each.
- Runtime (inference) pools (pilot): 4 x A10G equiv (8 GB GPU memory usable for model shards, target throughput ~120 tokens/sec per GPU for target model), 2 x CPU-only nodes for pre/post-processing.
- Batch/embeddings: 1 x A100 equiv on isolated node with dedicated NVME for sharding and intermediate storage.
- Storage: 2 TB model store on fast NVMe per GPU node; NFS-backed snapshot store for checkpoints and metrics with 99.9% availability.
- Network: 10GbE connectivity between runtime nodes and customer storage; sub-ms within-rack, <5ms cross-rack.
- Headroom: reserve 20% spare capacity for autoscaling buffer.

Terraform module notes (practical tips and overrides):
- Use our terraform modules/oauth_private_controlplane module with override var control_plane_internal_subnet to place control plane in private subnet. Avoid enabling public egress for control-plane nodes; use NAT gateways.
- Set var runtime_gpu_profile = "a10g-sliced" for pilot; production will replace with "a100-iso" when batch runs are validated.
- Use local-exec hooks sparingly; prefer remote-exec via our bootstrap agent for idempotency.
- State backends: require remote S3 backend with DynamoDB state locking (customer to provide S3 bucket in cross-account role). Documented example in linked GH PR.
- KMS integration: terraform module expects kms_key_id string. For CloudHSM, supply an alias ARN created by the customer; we wire KMS grants to the control plane IAM role during apply.

Upgrade and cutover plan (high level):
Pre-cutover (T-14 days):
- Confirm IP allocations and peering/VPN windows with Northbridge netops.
- Run terraform plan in staging; validate module outputs and IAM policies.
- Provision control plane in customer staging VPC in read-only mode.
- Validate KMS grants and test sample decrypt/encrypt via control-plane pods.

Cutover weekend (T-0 to T+2):
Day 0 (pre-door close):
- Freeze changes to Northbridge infra.
- Run final terraform apply for control plane HA.
- Bootstrap runtime pool with 2 GPUs; run internal smoke tests (latency, model load, KV cache priming).
- Enable canary route: 5% traffic to new runtime for 2 hours, then 25% for 4 hours if OK.
- Start embedding job in isolated batch node (dry run).

Day 1 (ramp):
- Increase runtime pool to target count, monitor token throughput and 95th latency.
- Run load tests using customer test harness: ramp to 50% of forecasted peak and hold for 30 minutes.
- If metrics within thresholds, shift traffic to new environment in 10% increments.

Rollback criteria and steps:
- If 95th latency > 200ms for > 10 minutes, or error rate increases by > 3x baseline: execute rollback.
- Rollback process: revert routing to prior endpoints, scale down new runtime nodes gracefully, snapshot logs and metrics, and open immediate postmortem channel.

Operational runbook snippets (to be converted to pager playbooks):
- Node replacement: drain pods, replace instance via terraform node_pool_count adjustment, verify model caches rehydrate.
- Model rollout: tag model images with semantic version, roll by canary, and run quality checks against golden prompt set stored in customer S3.
- Cost control: enable burst-to-hosted fallback for non-sensitive requests to reduce peak reserved capacity usage.

Security and compliance notes:
- Data never leaves customer network unless explicit export is enabled. Logging endpoints are customer-managed ELK.
- KMS/HSM: require attestation that key rotation policy is compatible with our control-plane grant model.
- Audit: enable control-plane request tracing and retain token-level billing for 90 days in customer storage.

Open questions for Northbridge (actionable items):
- Confirm preferred GPU instance families and whether quotas for A100 variants exist.
- Approve scheduled maintenance window for cutover weekend (we recommend Saturday 00:00-08:00 local).
- Provide CloudHSM alias ARN and IAM role for S3 state backend.
- Clarify whether nightly embedding jobs can be scheduled to avoid peak business hours.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpected network flapping during VPN cutover. Mitigation: schedule warm standby, use dual-path peering and test failover ahead of time.
- Risk: Model load times exceed expectation for cold starts. Mitigation: pre-warm with KV cache priming and smaller keep-alive interval.

Appendix: quick terraform snippets (conceptual, run in sandbox):
- module "control_plane" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//oauth_private_controlplane"
    control_plane_internal_subnet = "10.12.1.0/24"
    kms_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111:key/xxxxxxxx"
  }

- node pool override example:
  variable "runtime_gpu_profile" { default = "a10g-sliced" }

Next steps and owners:
- Action: Confirm GPU quota and maintenance window. Owner: Northbridge netops contact (assigned). Due: 2025-01-17.
- Action: Security review for KMS/CloudHSM granting model. Owner: Renee Martinez (redwood security). Due: 2025-01-20.
- Action: Finalize terraform state bucket cross-account role. Owner: Jinsoo Park. Due: 2025-01-24.

Notes to self: convert this draft into a formal runbook with checkboxes and precise CLI commands once all open questions answered. Keep this file as the canonical draft until T-7 days before cutover.

End of draft.
